items.detail: Three Australian stories told properly (what happened, why it matters, what's next), then a one-minute round-up of everything else in a sentence each, instead of six to nine stories at similar length.
items.title: A shorter, sharper Australia segment

items.detail: A box on the answer page where you can say you're away (like Brisbane this weekend). The show then uses that city's weather, a walk there instead of the Green Square commute, and local weekend ideas, until the date you give.
items.title: A 'Where are you?' box for travel

items.detail: Each Friday the answer page offers three candidates for Monday's Retro Game of the Week (one safe bet, one like the last game you liked, one wildcard), and you tap the one you fancy. After Demon's Crest came out mixed, this lets you steer.
items.title: Pick next week's retro game

items.detail: If no weekly task file arrives from your Mac's Sunday sync, Monday's answer page suggests a task for the week (for example the radish spawn, or a first farmhouse interior) and you tap the one you want, so the game thread always has a real goal.
items.title: A backup weekly task for Lanternfall

summary: Two episodes were rated this week: lore scored 5 both times and opening and world reached 5, while Australia dropped to 3 and the workshop sat at 3 then 4. You liked every story you voted on, finished Thursday's challenge, watched and liked Lady Snowblood, and called Demon's Crest mixed. So the show keeps lore and the game thread at the centre, tells fewer Australian stories more fully, and keeps the workshop to one evening job.
